Ukraine updates: Russian attack 'one of largest,' Zelenskyy says
Published November 20, 2026last updated November 20, 2026
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched one of the largest aerial attacks since the invasion began. Poland has said its airspace was violated in the process. Follow DW.
What you need to know
- Zelenskyy said the Russian attack included 400 drones and more than 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles
- At least 8 people were killed and several bridges and energy facilities were hit
- Poland said it's airspace was violated during the Russian attack
Below you can follow the latest updates from Russia's war in Ukraine on Friday, 20th November:
Ukraine says dozens of Russian oil and defense targets hit in past 50 days
The commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, Robert "Magyar" Brovdi said that his forces had hit 40 Russian oil facilities and defense industry targets in the past 50 days.
Brovdi said via the Telegram that among those targets, five of them had been hit more than once.
He went on to say that the Dorogobuzh chemical plant in Russia's Smolensk region was struck on November 10 and November 20.
Ukraine has managed to adapt on the battlefield with the use of drone technology which has allowed hundreds of drone sorties, in some cases deep inside Russian territory, on a daily basis.
Zelenskyy says overnight Russian attacks 'one of the largest'
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine was targeted by more than 400 drones and more than 110 missiles, 27 of which he said were ballistic missiles.
"The Russians spread this attack across many cities and regions of Ukraine. Absolutely all the targets were ordinary civilian infrastructure – things that literally sustain people’s lives," Zelenskyy said in a detailed post on social media platform X.
Zelenskyy listed what had been hit during the overnight strikes
- Energy facilities, substations and power lines, which Zelenskyy said nuclear facilities depended on
- Logistics and bridges across the Dnipro, three were reportedly struck
- Regular residential buildings damaged
- Zelenskyy says Russians used missiles with cluster warheads and described it as "one of the largest attacks"
He accused Russia of carrying out second strikes on targets that had already been hit, in so-called "double-tap strikes."
"People had essentially already been killed by the time specialists were inspecting the initial damage to the facilities, as the Russians were carrying out double-tap strikes," Zelenskyy said.
Most Russian missiles reportedly intercepted
Zelenskyy said that in all 79 cruise missiles had been intercepted and that fighter jets had been scrambled to deal with the aerial threats involving F-16s, Mirages and MiGs.
"Ballistic missiles are, unfortunately, much more difficult to deal with, and that depends not on our capabilities but on the supply of missiles by our partners," Zelenskyy said.
Ukraine's leader called for a "clear response" from the global community.
It is important that our partners not only issue statements in support of Ukraine and Ukrainians, but also follow through on specific agreements on air defense," Zelenskyy said.
He pointed out the timing of the latest attacks and said Putin launched them "in a highly demonstrative manner – following weak meetings in China."
"Russia is trying to compensate for its military and diplomatic impotence with precisely this kind of terror, precisely these attacks on life," Zelenskyy said.
Ukraine death toll rises to 8 after Russian bombardment
Ukrainian officials said that the death toll has risen to at least 8 following an overnight Russian aerial bombardment.
Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said six of the eight people killed were in Kyiv. Two deaths were also reported at a railway station in the western Ukrainian city of Lviv.
Ukraine's Air Force said Russia had launched 84 cruise missiles in the attack, adding that almost all of them were destroyed.
An unspecified number of ballistic missiles and more than 400 attack drones were also reported to have been destroyed.
Poland's defense chief confirms Russian attack on Ukraine 'impacted' Poland
Poland's Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said that several Russian flying objects entered Polish airspace during recent air attacks on Ukraine.
"Russian long-range aviation was operating, launching both Kinzhal and Kh-101 missiles, as well as a large number of jet-powered drones and conventional drones. … This Russian Federation attack on Ukrainian territory, which also had an impact on the Republic of Poland, was one of the largest since the beginning of Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine," the Defense Ministry quoted Kosiniak-Kamysz as saying.
It comes after Polish prosecutors reported earlier that a flying object had crashed in Poland's eastern Lublin region.
Polish officials said it had taken place during heavy Russian airstrikes on neighbouring Ukraine.
In July, a missile entered Polish airspace and crashed in the same region near the village of Tarnawa Kolonia.
According to the Polish government, it was a Russian CH-101 cruise missile.
Poland probing 'violations' of airspace at three locations
Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said that investigations were taking place at three sites after reporting that Polish airspace had been violated.
"In connection with violations of Polish airspace, authorities are conducting operations at three locations: Rudnik nad Sanem, Molodycz and Nowy Lipowiec (Lublin Province)," he said in a post on social media platform X.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that he had convened a meeting of senior government and military officials along with the heads of security services in a post on X. He said there was currently no danger from the air.

Deaths and damage reported in Russian missile strikes on Kyiv
Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko said that a Russian missile bombardment in Kyiv has killed at least three people and injured 13 others.
Klitschko said in a post on Telegram that three bridges had also been damaged following the strikes on Ukraine's capital.
Experts would only be able to give a proper assessment of the damage caused to the structures once the aerial threat had ended, Klitschko added.
"Given the difficult traffic conditions between the left and right banks of the capital, I ask residents not to leave the city by private car unless absolutely necessary," the mayor said.
Klitschko also appealed to employers to allow remote-working arrangements, where possible.
Bridges have been key targets in Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine, but Kyiv's forces have managed to hit the Kerch bridge multiple times this week in what is being seen as a major psychological blow to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
He warned of a harsh response after the bridge linking occupied Crimea with mainland Russia was struck three times this week.
One of the archways and a section of roadway was destroyed in the attack.
Putin said he expected Moscow's response to be "far more painful" than the damage Ukraine had caused to the Kerch bridge.
Welcome to our coverage
Just a day after moves by world leaders to get warring parties to the negotiation table in the form of two summits — one in China, the other in Berlin — Russia has continued with its nightly attacks on Ukraine.
Kyiv has been been targeted by Russian missiles with local officials reporting deaths as a result and damage to at least three bridges.
The latest strikes follow ominous warnings from Russian President Vladimir Putin that Moscow's response would be "far more painful" than the damage done to the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia.
